generation.explanation: A secant line goes through two points on the curve, P = (x₀, f(x₀)) and Q = (x₀+h, f(x₀+h)). Its slope is the difference quotient [f(x₀+h) − f(x₀)] / h. As h gets smaller, Q slides along the curve toward P, and the secant (orange) turns until it matches the tangent line (green). In the limit h → 0, the secant slope equals the derivative f′(x₀). The animation shrinks h automatically. You can then use the sliders to change h and x₀, or press the button to watch the limit again.
